articleTitle: An improved adi-fdtd method with lower splitting error
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Based on the Crank-Nicolson (CN) scheme, an improved alternating direction implicit finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method is proposed. By introducing local correction, the proposed method reduces the splitting error while the unconditional stability and computational efficiency are maintained. Theoretical analyses are given.

articleTitle: Polarization signal components estimate in weather radar
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: New approach to use polarimetry for turbulence intensity estimate is proposed. It is based on estimation of the energetic characteristics of turbulent polarization spectrum. The proposed approach can be realized as a radar system that allows estimating the energetic characteristics of a set of polarization components of the received radar signal. The layout of a radar system for polarization components estimation is developed. Such approach can increase the informativity of weather radar systems relatively to obtaining information about factors that are the origin of changing polarization of reflected signal.

articleTitle: Estimation of thickness of subsurface air layer by neuron network technology application to reflected microwave signal
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Neuron network technology application to subsurface air layer thickness estimation is considered. The envelope of time-domain signal was used as input data. The three-layered neuron network with backpropagation and sigmoid (S-shaped) activation function of neurons was chosen. The comparison with results of correlation method is presented.

articleTitle: Evolution of radiopulses radiated by Hertz's dipole in vacuum
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Properties of the fields and power descriptions are considered. It is shown that the form of radiopulses in a distant area is determined by a derivative from the form of impulse of current, given on Hertzpsilas dipole. Power descriptions of the electromagnetic field are proportional to the square of derivative from the form of impulse of current, given on Hertzpsilas dipole.

articleTitle: Determination of parameters of fractional-rational model using method of quasisolution searching
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The opportunity of increase of accuracy and stability of fractional-rational approximation at the expense of use of quasisolution concept has been considered. The algorithm of quasisolution searching on the basis of increasing model order is presented. The accuracy of the suggested method has been analyzed and its application for processing the resonant response is considered.

articleTitle: Two notched band two post waveguide section
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper a two post rectangular waveguide section is presented. The posts are located side by side in a guide cross-section. The waveguide section provides a frequency response with two independently controllable notched bands. Each rejection frequency is tuned by a changing the height of one of two posts, whereas a rejection bandwidth is defined mainly by a post width.

articleTitle: Numerical calculation of the lyapunov exponent for the logistic MAP
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Chaotic maps can be used to describe the behavior of dynamical systems and they are characterized by a parameter. The logistic map (LM) is a chaotic map very used in different areas. In the analysis of the dynamical system an important feature is the system stability, which can be determined using the Lyapunov Exponent (LE). In this paper two ways to compute numerically the LE for the LM are shown. In the first alternative, the Birkhoffpsilas Ergodic Theorem (BET) and the orbit produced by the LM are used. In the second alternative, the stationary distribution rho<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">est</sub> of the LM is estimated using the first derived of the logistic function and the central values of each interval in the partition used in the estimation.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of permittivity profile for stratified dielectric material: Gel’fand-Levitan and Newton-Kantorovich methods
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The improved variant of the Gelpsilafand-Levitan method demonstrating faster speed of reconstruction in comparison with the ldquoclassicalrdquo one is proposed. A modification of the Newton-Kantorovich method for permittivity profile reconstruction of stratified dielectric is proposed. Factors having influence on duration and precision of profile reconstruction by these two methods are noted.

articleTitle: Steganographic communication channel using audio signals
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Using MP3 and WAV audio digital signals an algorithm to build a steganographic communication channel is presented. This algorithm is conformed by the insertion and extraction procedures and it use direct sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) to insert confidential (subliminal) information in MP3 and WAV audio digital signals. Evaluation tests were applied to the different steganographic communications channels. According with the obtained results this algorithm can be used to property or exploitation right protection of the audio digital signals.

articleTitle: Circular Polarized Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna using single probe feeds
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (RDRAs) which providing circular polarization (CP) using single probe feeds are studied. A new technique for CP achievement is presented. This technique proposed that by modifying the RDRAs in suitable way, the fundamental mode of conventional rectangular DRA splits into two near-degenerate orthogonal resonant modes and CP is obtained. The proposed antennas are numerically investigated using finite element method (FEM). The investigation indicates that the radiation patterns of all antennas are remaining broadside throughout the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic theory of nanodimensional antennas for terahertz, infrared and optical regimes
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An electrodynamical theory of the vibrator nanoantenna based on the different types of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has been presented. The theory covers a wide frequency range from terahertz to optical frequencies. It is based on the quantum-mechanical description of the CNT conductivity. The boundary-value electrodynamical problem has been formulated using the effective boundary conditions method and has been solved by the integral equations technique. As a result, a number of general properties of CNT-based nanoantennas have been revealed. These properties are very promising for potential applications in nanoelectronics, high resolution near field optical microscopy, thermal microscopy, etc.

articleTitle: Fano resonance of waves in periodic slabs
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We investigate Fano-type anomalous transmission of energy of plane waves across lossless slab scatterers with periodic structure in the presence of non-robust guided modes. Our approach is based on rigorous analytic perturbation of the scattering problem near a guided mode and applies to very general structures, continuous and discrete.

articleTitle: Application of MAS and FDTD for the design of 2-D EBG resonator antennas and dielectric/guided lenses
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The electromagnetic synthesis and optimization of microwave focusing systems requires the development of specific CAD tools with appropriate characteristics (accuracy, computation time, etc.). The purpose of this paper is to benchmark two 2D numerical methods, namely the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) and the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. Several relevant test structures (integrated lens antennas, EBG resonator antennas, constrained lenses) have been designed to assess the impact of the intrinsic features of both algorithms (e.g. stair-case approximation in FDTD, kind and location of the auxiliary sources in MAS) upon the numerical results.

articleTitle: Physical properties of narrow slots in a rectangular waveguide with dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Narrow slots cut in rectangular waveguides with dielectric layers parallel to the waveguide narrow or broad walls are considered. The theory elaborated by the authors for such slots is applied to numerical studying of their physical properties. The resonance properties and energetic parameters of the longitudinal and transversal slots are investigated in one-mode regime of the waveguide. The most interesting regularities caused by variation of the layers permittivity epsiv are discussed.

articleTitle: Adaptation of sample myriad tunable parameter to characteristics of SαS distribution
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Processes obeying heavy-tailed symmetric alpha-stable (SalphaS) distributions have been shown to describe well many natural phenomena in radio engineering, acoustics, communications, etc. For processing such data, one needs to apply robust estimators and the methods based on a sample myriad are considered quasi-optimal ones. Sample myriad estimation requires setting a tunable parameter k. However, only quite approximate and impractical recommendations concerning its selection exist. Thus, in this paper we consider some approaches to deal with setting k in practical applications. It is shown that they are to be adaptive to data sample scale and tail heaviness.

articleTitle: Some exact solutions of transient problems of electrodynamics in spherical coordinate system obtained by symmetry analysis of Klein-Gordon-Fock equation
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Applying separation of variables to Maxwell equations in time domain one arrives to Klein-Gordon-Fock equation that describes radial wave propagation. The separation parameter for free space case has special form allowing the general solution to be found in exact form. For arbitrary separation parameter, which occurs in analysis of conical lines, the general solution is not suitable for calculations since it contains fractional derivatives. In this paper we obtain several families of exact solutions for this case using method of symmetry analysis of the equation.

articleTitle: Mathematical model for spiraphase-type infinite reflective array based on slot ring resonators with pin diode switches
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Mathematical model has been developed to predict the characteristics of spiraphase-type phased array based on slot ring resonators with p-i-n diode switches. It is demonstrated that this array can redirect an incident circularly polarized wave in the directions determined by reflection elevation angles up to 60deg in a 20% frequency band with total loss less than 3.5 dB.

articleTitle: A surfacewave excitation by a finite phased planewaveguide array with an impedance flange
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper the surface wave excitation by the finite phased array of plane waveguides with an impedance flange has been theoretically investigated. The surface waves excited by the array has been considered as superposition of surface waves exited by each waveguide. Mutual coupling between waveguide apertures has been taking into account using variational principle in the single-mode approximation. Some numerical results for the system of two waveguides has been analyzed.

articleTitle: Correlation properties of electromagnetic field generated by emitters with random orientation
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The necessity of more thorough description of electromagnetic field is substantiated for the problems of quantum optics. An attempt to construct the correlation functions of emission generated by a superfluorescent system of Dicke type is done. Operator evolution equations for a system of two-level emitters interacting with electromagnetic field lead to quantum analogues of Maxwell equations. Reduced description method applied to the superfluorescent process allows to find parameters characterizing the field fluctuations and some generalizations of matter equations.

articleTitle: Calculation of the reflection matrix in the plane waveguide by scanning screen method
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The possibility of calculation of coefficients of the reflection matrix partially describing inhomogeneous in the plane waveguide with metallic sides by bounded number of characteristics of the reflected field is studied. To receive the additional information it is proposed to use a thin conducting screen placed in front of the investigated heterogeneity.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of guided-mode resonances in planar doubly-periodic dielectric structures
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper the scattering characteristics are calculated with the technique based on the volume integral equations for polarization currents. Full-wave analysis is performed. A silicon-on-sapphire periodic structure is used to study the guided-mode resonances in plane-wave excitation conditions. Numerical computations for the reflection spectral resonances are presented for both weak and strong layer modulations. Spectral stability of resonances as a function of angle of incidence is investigated.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf analysis of grooved coaxial waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A Wiener-Hopf analysis is provided for the propagation of the dominant TEM mode in a coaxial waveguide with a dielectric filled groove on the outer conductor. Some graphical results showing the effects of the groove depth and the dielectric permittivity of the material filling the groove are presented.

articleTitle: On the ideal gain of a radiating element in a planar array
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The well known formula for the ideal gain of an element in an infinite planar array is derived with methodical purposes on the basis of the general antenna theory applied to periodic structures. The derivation shows that the ideal element gain is a secondary array parameter determined by the ideal element pattern despite the fact that, historically, the formula for it was written earlier than it was done for the ideal array element pattern.

articleTitle: Characterization and analysis of left-handed chiral materials
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this study, the analysis of the left-handed chiral material is presented. The possibility of the negative phase velocity, negative and positive propagation constants, and basic electromagnetic properties of the mentioned medium are also studied. In the analysis, the characterization of left-handed chiral material is given in detail. Some numerical results are also provided to validate the formulation found in the analysis.

articleTitle: Convergence and oscillations in the method of auxiliary sources
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: When one applies the method of auxiliary sources to scattering problems involving perfect conductors, one first seeks fictitious auxiliary currents located inside the conductor, and then determines the field from these currents. For a simple two-dimensional problem involving an infinite circular cylinder illuminated by an electric current filament, it has recently been shown analytically that it is possible to have divergent auxiliary currents (to make this statement precise, one must properly normalize the currents), together with a convergent field. It was also shown - through numerical investigations - that the aforementioned divergence appears as abnormal, rapid oscillations. In the present paper, we investigate such phenomena in more detail, with particular emphasis on oscillations: For a perfectly conducting ground plane illuminated by an electric current filament, we once again demonstrate the possibility of having divergent, oscillating currents producing a convergent field. We develop an asymptotic formula for the oscillating current values, which sheds light on the nature of the oscillations. We also discuss roundoff errors. The present study is to a great extent analytical, with the analytical predictions confirmed and supplemented by numerical results.

articleTitle: Sub-wavelength photonics - challenges and research opportunities
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The talk discusses the challenges in sub-wavelength photonics, and it reports on the research agenda of a starting European project COST Action MP0702: towards functional sub-wavelength photonic structures.

articleTitle: Transient radiation from the open end of circular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The transient radiation from the open end of a circular waveguide is considered by analytical and direct numerical methods. The radiation of short pulse from the aperture is considered by calculation of special time form of field by means of modal basis method. The method permits to solve the problem of pulse evolution for positive and negative time with the use of Laplace transform by construction of operator of propagation. The method of correction of pulse distortion on aperture is suggested on the base of properties of operator of propagation in waveguide. The control of pulse form of field on aperture is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Calculation method for non-ideally conducting object with thin dielectric envelope
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The scattered electromagnetic field calculation method for object with non-ideally conducting surface and thin dielectric envelope is considered. The base of method is the calculation of the field scattered by non-ideally conducting object in far and near zones of scatterer and the estimation for contribution of dielectric envelope to the field scattered by this object in far zone. The calculation results for object in thin dielectric envelope are given.

articleTitle: Determination of antenna characteristics via system of S-parameters
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A new way of antenna characteristics determination via S-parameters matrix, in which radiation characteristics of antenna are considered as a result of electromagnetic interaction between the transmitting antenna and omnipolarization receiving antenna, is presented in the report. A correspondence table of antenna electromagnetic parameters in traditional form and ones represented in terms of S-parameters is given as well.

articleTitle: On the radiation efficiency of a dense array antenna shaping a sector radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An infinite linear periodic array of densely arranged radiators having small transverse dimensions is considered. It is analytically shown that the radiation efficiency of the array with non-uniform excitation corresponding to shaping a sector radiation pattern is determined by averaging the mismatch efficiency of the same array excited with identical amplitudes and linearly progressing phases, over the region of scanning coinciding with the region occupied by the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Plasma oscillations in field-effect transistor arrays
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Terahertz (THz) plasmonic spectra of field-effect transistor (FET) arrays are discussed for two different types of FET arrays: (i) FET array with a common channel and a large-area grating gate, and (ii) array of FET units with separate channels and combined intrinsic source and drain contacts. It is shown that the coupling between plasmons and THz radiation in the FET array can be strongly enhanced as compared to a single-unit FET due to excitation of the cooperative plasmon mode distributed over the entire area of the FET array. The higher-order plasmon modes revealing the plasmon resonances at frequencies up to 20 THz can be excited much more effectively in the array of FET units with separate channels and combined source and drain contacts.

articleTitle: New closed form expressions for layered media green’s functions
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The rational function fitting method (RFFM) is a powerful alternative to discrete complex images (DCIM) in the derivation of closed-form expressions of spatial domain Greenpsilas functions (SDGF) for multilayered media. However, former implementations of that method are inaccurate when the far field is dominated by the continuous spectrum instead of by surface waves. In this paper the authors modify the original implementation of RFFM in order to overcome that problem.

articleTitle: On transmitting of electromagnetic wave through anisotropic layer
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The two-dimensional problem on transmitting of the perpendicular polarized electromagnetic wave through anisotropic plane layer is reduced to the linear algebraic set of equations for Fourier transforms of the auxiliary boundary functions by the over-determined boundary value problem method.

articleTitle: Modelling of shielding effectiveness using small samples of tested materials
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The limitations of a widely used setup consisting of two horn antennas for evaluation of shielding effectiveness is investigated. The proposed method can provide a non-destructive characterization of small bulk materials and grid structures with sizes comparable to the wavelength of the scanning signal. As it is proved by the numerical modeling the suggested measurement setup inevitably introduces some spurious diffraction. Nevertheless, the use of statistical approximation allows effectively retrieving the shielding effectiveness of studied samples, which is validated by the analytical results.

articleTitle: Optimised compact 90° optical waveguide bend
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A 90deg photonic crystal bend is designed using an approach that combines recent advances in fast simulation algorithms, iterative matrix solvers and genetic algorithm optimisation routines.

articleTitle: A comparison between the FDTD convolutional PML and reradiating boundary conditions for simple 3D test problem
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper we provide a field termination performance comparison between convolutional PML and reradiating FDTD boundary conditions for simple numerical experiment. It is shown that for the 3D case a simple stackable re-radiating boundary condition (R-RBC) competes with a convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML). The essence of the R-RBC which based on Field Teleportation technique, is to invoke the principle of equivalent sources using FDTDpsilas discrete definition of the curl to copy any field propagating in one FDTD domain to a finite region of another domain. In this paper we apply this technique of field teleportation to the original 3D domain itself to create a transparent boundary across which any outward traveling FDTD field produces an exact negative copy of itself causing self-canceling. Relatively thin (5 cells) RRBC readily yields absorption of the order of -80 dB in 3D ldquoanechoic chamberrdquo test whereas CPML shows similar performance for a 20-cells layer.

articleTitle: Superresolution via extrapolation with constraints on signal duration
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Method of signal extrapolation in frequency domain for improvement of resolution in time domain is proposed. The main idea of this method is use of concept of duration of signal through formulation of non-energy constraints, when there is a priori information about finiteness of signal support in time domain. Unlike traditional extrapolation techniques no strict model of extrapolated data is required, as well as no exact information about signal support in Fourier conjugate domain must be provided. Developed approach is investigated through numerical simulations and applied for processing of multifrequency data of complex reflection coefficient of dielectric layered structure.

articleTitle: Desensitization of unstructured transmssion line modeling simulations to mesh characteristics
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Flexible simulation solvers are paramount for the development of a wide range of modern technologies. Numerical techniques complement computationally efficient analytical approaches and offer ease of use and applicability to a wide range of applications. The Transmission Line Modeling Method has recently been extended to the domain of tetrahedral mesh descriptions of structure geometry and this presentation discusses a number of recent advances that affect its practical deployment.

articleTitle: Two aspects in lossy compression of hypespectral aviris images
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Hyperspectral images formed by AVIRIS imager are often compressed for data transmission and storage. For this purpose, both lossless and lossy compression methods can be used, but the latter are able to provide considerably larger compression ratios. Lossy compression can be done effectively in automatic manner with grouping of sub-bands and setting the quantization step depending upon estimates of noise variance for sub-band images. In this paper we show how to select this quantization step for each group of sub-bands with providing a proper trade-off between losses (distortions) introduced and attainable compression ratio for simple and more realistic models of noise.

articleTitle: Band-pass filters on thin diaphragms in waveguides of complex cross section
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The method of synthesis of filters on transverse discontinuities in waveguides of complex cross-sections is described. As a basic filter model the model of catenation of reentrant cavities is used where each resonator presented by the part of regular transmission line between two equal transverse discontinuities. The band pass filters with quarter-wavelength links and direct coupling on thin metal diaphragms in two ridge and trough waveguides are synthesized by the described technique.

articleTitle: Scattering by parallel conducting rods for cylindrical wave incidence using floquet modes
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, the Floquet-mode technique and method of moments are compared for calculating the near-field scattering by a large number of parallel conducting rods in front of a line source. In order to apply the Floquet-mode technique, a line source excitation is assumed as a spectrum of one-dimensional problems (plane-wave incident). Each rod is modeled by an array of thin wires subject to the ldquosame surface areardquo rule of thumb. It is observed that the Floquet-mode technique is computationally more efficient than the method of moments for a large number of rods.

articleTitle: Simulations of nanometric optical circuits by surface plasmon polariton gap waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The guided waves in the surface plasmon polariton gap waveguide (SPGW) excited through an aperture have been investigated by the three-dimensional simulations using a volume integral equation. The complex propagation constants of the guided waves have been calculated from the simulated optical fields using the least-squares fitting. Applications of SPGWs to nanosize E-plane planar optical circuits are also demonstrated.

articleTitle: On the solutions of the electrical impedance equation, applying quaternionic analysis and pseudoanalytic function theory
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We review the state of the art of solutions for the electrical impedance equation div (γ gradu) = 0 where the function div γ = σ + iωε is the admitivity, σ denotes the conductivity, ε is the frequency, ε is the permittivity, i is the imaginary unit, and u denotes the electric potential. When γ is a function of three spatial variables, we show how to rewrite the equation into a stationary Schrödinger equation, and using elements of quaternionic analysis, we study one method for factorizing this Schrödinger equation’s operator into two first-order differential operators. For the two-dimensional case we show that the electrical impedance equation is equivalent to a particular Vekua equation, and using recent discoveries in Pseudoanalytic Function Theory, we analyze the structure of its solutions. We broach how to solve the inverse Calderon problem in the plane, and finally we mention the concepts that allows us to express the general solution of the electrical equation through Taylor series in formal powers.

articleTitle: On the efficient computation of the Green’s function for doubly periodic structures by using the Kunmer’s method of higher orders
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An auxiliary function in the form of standing spherical waves with attenuation is proposed in the Kummerpsilas method for accelerating the convergence of the spectral series representing the Greenpsilas function of doubly periodic structures in free space. Expressions for the amplitude and phase constants of the auxiliary waves versus their attenuation constant are derived, at which the spectral difference series converges in the worst case as the Floquet mode propagation constant in the power of minus 5, 9, and 13 for the cases of using one, two, and three auxiliary waves, respectively.

articleTitle: Arbitrary shaped hollow resonators and waveguides modeling. Analytical regularization method
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Mathematically strong and efficient approach for simulation of resonators and waveguides of arbitrary profile is suggested. The approach is based on new implementation of Analytical Regularization Method. Numerical results of E-polarized wave diffraction by waveguide resonant structures demonstrate the method efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of multimode optical fibre sensors
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The numerical modeling of the multimode optical-fiber evanescent-field sensors is described. The work is focused on sensors which employ essentially multimode plastic optical fibers and plastic optical detection elements. The ray-tracing model is employed which is complemented with mode coupling and mode-dependent attenuation obtained from measurements. It is shown that in the case of relatively short optical fibers such as used in sensors, the characteristics of particular light source, evolution of light distribution along the optical fibers, and finite non-homogeneity of plastic material have a significant effect on sensor characteristics.

articleTitle: One-dimensional anisotropic photonic crystals based on anisotropic porous silicon
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The model for description of one-dimensional anisotropic photonic crystals based on anisotropic porous silicon is proposed. The finite difference technique is applied for the scattering matrix parameter computation. Reflectance spectra for two orthogonal polarizations of the incident plane wave are calculated. The dependence of the shift of the spectral position of the photonic band gap edges on the orientation of the optical axis of the structure with respect to the incidence plane of s- or p-polarization incident plane wave is studied.

articleTitle: Pseudoharmonic middle-domain functions with smooth envelope in moment method for quasiperiodic open structures
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Phenomena of coupling of wave paraxial beam and quasisurface wave at perfectly conducting plane with segment of spatially oscillating surface impedance is considered. Integral equation for perturbed current distribution is obtained. Method of moments is used. Solution was expanded in terms of pseudoharmonic middle-domain (long subdomain) basis functions. Smooth envelopes in form of a combination of atomic functions and the Lagrangian interpolating polynomials were applied. Results for some types of test functions were compared.

articleTitle: Plasmonic metamaterials: From modelling to applications
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Plasmonic metamaterials based on metal-dielectric nanostructures exhibit unique optical properties and find numerous applications in such diverse areas as optical communications, chemo- and bio-sensing, high-density data storage and many others. These properties can be tailored to specific applications and requirements by changing structural and dielectric parameters of the constituents. Here we discuss the design principles, modeling and applications of two types of plasmonic metamaterials based on plsamonic crystals and plasmonic nanorod arrays.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic analysis of carbon nanotube antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The solution of the boundary problem of diffraction and excitation of system of carbon nanotubes-vibrators is reduced to solving of the integral equation with a logarithmic kernel. After regularization, integral equations were solved by means of collocation method. The character of behavior of the current on the vibratorpsilas ends was considered. The existence of resonances at the frequency range 0.1-1.0THz was shown.

articleTitle: A vectorial variational mode solver and its application to piecewise constant and diffused waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A Variational Vectorial Mode Solver for 3-D dielectric waveguides with arbitrary 2-D cross-sections is proposed. It is based on expansion of each component of a mode profile as a superposition of some a priori defined functions defined on one coordinate axis times some unknown continuous coefficient functions, defined on the other axis. By applying a variational restriction procedure the unknown coefficient functions are determined as an optimum approximation of the true vectorial mode profile. A couple of examples illustrate the performance of the method.

articleTitle: Fractional dual parabolic cylindrical reflector
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Geometrical optics (GO) fields of a fractional dual parabolic cylindrical reflector have been studied around the focusing region using Maslovpsilas method. GO fields contain both co- and cross-polarized components. Considering perfect electric conductor as original case, magnitudes of the GO fields do not depend upon the fractional parameter. For impedance boundary reflector as original case, the field components depend upon the fractional parameter. Dependence of co-polarized and cross-polarized field components in different ranges of surface impedance has been studied.

articleTitle: Application of space domain integral equation approach for electromagnetic analysis of microstrip structures
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The paper is devoted to determination of the impedance matrix elements for the T-junction microstrip structure. The analytical and numerical-analytical approaches for investigation of the full-wave radiation in such discontinuity are combined. The components of electrical field are determined from the respective Pocklingtonpsilas equation. Application of the Galerkinpsilas procedure allows to receive the respective matrix equation. The elements of received matrix are calculated by the combination of the analytical and numerical integration; the network parameters of structure are calculated by these elements.

articleTitle: Development of a new efficient numerical method, creation of package of program and making experimental setup for recognition of latent objects
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The primary objectives of this paper are creation of the program package for determination of shape and position of metallic and/or dielectric bodies embedded within a dielectric media, determination of dielectric parameters of the body suppose. The main goal is construction of a high-speed device for measurement and recording amplitude and phase information of the electromagnetic wave over a two-dimensional surface, connected to the computer will realize the detection process using developed software.

articleTitle: Numerical method for calculation of the generalized natural modes of an inhomogeneous optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The eigenvalue problem for generalized natural modes of an inhomogeneous optical fiber without a sharp boundary is formulated as a problem for the set of time-harmonic Maxwell equations with Reichardt condition at infinity in the cross-sectional plane. The generalized eigenvalues of this problem are the complex propagation constants on a logarithmic Reimann surface. The original problem is reduced to a nonlinear spectral problem with Fredholm integral operator. Theorem on spectrum localization is proved, and then it is proved that the set of all eigenvalues of the original problem can only be a set of isolated points on the Reimann surface, ant it also proved that each eigenvalue depends continuously on the frequency and refraction index and can appear and disappear only at the boundary of the Reimann surface. The Galerkin method for numerical calculation of the generalized natural modes is proposed, and the convergence of the method is proved.

articleTitle: Circular polarized rectangular loop antenna over a mushroom-like EBG surface
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, a low profile dual loop wire antenna over an EBG surface is investigated for wideband circular polarization. A wideband mushroom-like EBG surface is used as the antenna ground plane. In comparison with a PEC ground plane, design of the antenna above an EBG ground plane results in 60% reduction of the structure thickness. It is shown that the axial ratio bandwidth (≪3dB) and return loss bandwidth (≪10dB) of the dual loop antenna above the designed EBG surface are 20% and 14%, respectively.

articleTitle: Cylindrical fresnel lenses
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Features of geometrical configuration of Fresnel lenses with cylindrical radiating surface as antenna elements are considered. The problem of diffraction is numerically solved with the aid of the method of the integral equations. The focal-domain fields of lenses, their radiation patterns, and frequency properties are determined.

articleTitle: Field oscillators in linear electromagnetic theory of plasma
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: On the basis of the Bogolyubov reduced description method, equations of motion for the description of the electromagnetic field in equilibrium plasma have been obtained. It is shown that these equations give the known results of the Vlasov theory with the self-consistent field.

articleTitle: Spectra for 1D magneto-photonic crystal with tri-layer cell interfaced with metallic structures at microwave band
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We study microwave spectra for a one-dimensional magneto-photonic crystal (MPC) with tri-layer cell (vacuum/ yttrium iron garnet (YIG) / quartz) interfaced with metallic structures (thin metallic slab or thin wire structure (TWS)). We show, non-propagating surface mode (so-called ldquomicrowave Tamm staterdquo) arises at interface between MPC and TWS as well as for metallic slab. These states result in a sharp peak in the transmission and reflection spectra of the system under study.

articleTitle: Special theory of relativity and universal boundary conditions on uniformly moving surfaces
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The knowledge of the boundary conditions, which interrelate the field values observed on different sides of interfaces between different bodies, has crucial importance for the study of the electromagnetic phenomena created by a given source configuration. During the last century these conditions were discussed rather extensively in cases when the boundaries are at rest with respect to the observer. When the boundary is in motion with respect to the observer, the situation is still rather obscure and causes to tough difficulties. For example, the shape of the boundary seems differently, in general, for an observer moving with it and for an observer to which it is in motion. Hence, it is not an exact approach to try to reveal the boundary conditions on a moving body by assuming that its geometrical shape is known beforehand. The correct approach is the derivation of the boundary relations first in a reference system which moves with the boundary and then to transform the relations into the reference system of the observer. This can be done by the principles of the Special Theory of Relativity if the motion is uniform. The present paper aims to this end for the most general case and derive the universal boundary conditions and compatibility relations. Some illustrative examples show how the compatibility relations are elaborated in obtaining the particular forms of the boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Improved method of remote sensing retrieval of sea water chlorophyll
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Method of satellite data correction, adjusting the standard atmospheric correction, is considered. Marine phytoplankton pigment concentrations were retrieved from SeaWiFS data using the correction proposed. Maps of chlorophyll distribution in region of Crimean South Coast were plotted, showing best correlation with biological data than when using standard methods.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction by a double-layer periodic grating of curvilinear strips
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Reflection and transmission characteristics of double-layer two-periodic gratings of perfectly conducting infinite strips with a complex shape are considered. Numerical analysis of electromagnetic wave diffraction by the structure was carried out by the integral equation method.

articleTitle: Expofunctional excitation in classical electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this article the essence of the phenomenon of selection of active power an electric circuit reactive elements is described. The main features arising in classical electrodynamics from application expofunctional excitation of an electromagnetic field are shown. The mechanism of the physical processes proceeding at excitation of physical vacuum by expofunctional strange source of a current is described.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of electromagnetic scattering by perfectly conducting surfaces of revolution
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The integro-differential equation (IDE) of a three-dimensional (3-D) electromagnetic ex citation problem of unclosed surfaces is numerically treated by means of the novel direct solver.

articleTitle: Quaternionic approach to electromagnetic
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In the present paper we give an overview of recent applications of quaternionic analysis techniques to different mathematical models of electromagnetic theory. In this contribution we explain a numerical method for solving electromagnetic scattering problems in chiral media with an unusual for three-dimensional models precision by the aid of biquaternionic fundamental solutions which to the difference of the usually utilized matrix fundamental solutions for the Maxwell equations enjoy some advantageous properties.

articleTitle: Geometry optimization of periodic screen cell with two orthogonal rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We consider the periodic screen with cell containing two rectangular slots with one offset relatively to the cellpsilas line of symmetry. Elements of reflection matrix and value of chirality measure in dependence of this offset are calculated. The optimal offset of slot in such periodic sell of thin enough screen is found. Additional checkup of chirality measure model is provided.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic pulse scattering by dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: General solution of the two-dimensional electromagnetic pulse scattering by a dielectric layer problems are considered. Expressions for fields of the localized source in an arbitrary point of space are written down. Numerical results for reflection and transmission coefficients of the primary pulse for various physical and geometrical parameters of scattering object are obtained.

articleTitle: Mode solvers and mode expansion methods for integrated photonics
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Principles of mode solvers for straight and circularly bent waveguides based on mode matching are briefly reviewed. Next, the principles of a bi-directional mode expansion propagation scheme based on harmonic expansion are presented and its performance assessed in comparison with some other approaches.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics analysis of substrate integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Effective technique of analysis of propagation and diffraction waves in periodical waveguides composed with rods of arbitrary cross-section was developed on the base of semi- inversion method. Accuracy of obtained results was proved by comparison calculated data with known ones for some waveguide configurations.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of the microstrip phased array of longitudinal printed radiators with adequate simulation of strip feed lines
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Full-wave solution of electromagnetic problem about lumped excitation microstrip phased array with longitudinal printed radiators has been obtained. Novelty of the offered mathematical model consists in the adequate description of a stripline feeder influence on characteristics of the microstrip array. It is reached by full-wave modeling, as a microstrip radiator of the phased antenna array, as that part of a stripline feeder which directly adjoins to antenna element of an array.

articleTitle: Interplay between the ray and mode effects in electromagnetic behavior of small-size hemielliptic dielectric lenses
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Focusing and resonance properties of two-dimensional (2-D) small-size hemielliptic lenses made of different materials are studied numerically in order to estimate the influence of internal reflections on the radiation characteristics of dielectric lens antennas (DLA). Accuracy of in-house made algorithms based on combination of geometrical and physical optics (GO, PO) and FDTD in the analysis of optical and modal effects in the behavior of such lenses is tested by comparison with the exact solution obtained using the Muller boundary integral equations (MBIE). The range of applicability for the approaches is discussed.

articleTitle: Modelling of transients in microcavities with time-varying material properties
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The object of this paper is to present an analytic-numeric approach to the 2D problem of electromagnetic field transformation caused by the time variation of material properties inside the circular resonator.

articleTitle: On eigenmodes of a spherical-mirror open resonator
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A mathematically rigorous analysis is given to eigenmodes of an open resonator (OR) with spherical mirrors in the case when the wavelength is comparable with the resonator size. The traditional eigenmode classification based on OR approximate models has been refined and essentially generalized.

articleTitle: The 2 × 2-matrix method for two-dimensional parametric system
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A two-dimensional parametric system with piecewise constant parameters is investigated in this paper. It is offered the accurate analytical method based on 2 times 2 matrix for study of such a system.

articleTitle: Excitation of a dielectric sphere by a radial electric dipole taking into account the spatial dispersion
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Excitation of dielectric sphere by radial electric dipole was studied with account spatial dispersion. Taking into account a spatial dispersion results in occurrence of the complementary E-type oscillations.

articleTitle: Investigation of complex wave propagation in the semiconductor layered periodic walls
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper is devoted to the problem of propagation of the waves with complex wave vector in periodic semiconductor-dielectric structure in the absence of and in the presence of the external magnetic field. The dispersion equation is investigated in the complex plane of longitudinal wave-vector component. The peculiarity of complex wave energy distribution is considered.

articleTitle: Modeling the scattering characteristics of complex-shaped dielectric bodies by the pattern equations method
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An efficient method is proposed for solving the problem of diffraction on dielectric bodies with a complex geometry. The initial problem is reduced to a system of algebraic equations by expanding the scattering patterns in vector angular spherical harmonics. It is shown that the method offers a high rate of convergence that weakly depends on the distances between them. The possibility of using the PEM for modeling the scattering characteristics of complex-shaped bodies is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Radiation condition in modal methods: Numerical implementation by means of complex coordinates transformations
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper show how to implement effectively the method of moments in the general framework of modal methods. It also used to generalized stretched coordinates in order to enhance spatial resolution on one hand and to introduce a radiation condition on the other hand. The modal methods and mode matching techniques are well established methods to solve waveguide and scattering problems. Such methods lead to an eigenvalue problem that is transformed into a numerical matrix eigenvalue problem by the method of moments.

articleTitle: A COMBINATION OF Dirichlet to Neumann operators and perfectly matched layers as boundary conditions for optical finite element simulations
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: By combining Dirichlet to Neumann (DtN) operators and Perfectly Matched Layers (PML’s) as boundary conditions on a rectangular domain on which the Helmholtz equation is solved, the disadvantages of both methods are greatly diminished. Due to the DtN operators, light may be accurately fluxed into the domain, while the PML’s absorb light that is reflected from the corners of the domain when only DtN boundaries are used.

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission of transverse — magnetic waves from anisotropic magnetoactive plate in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The propagation of electromagnetic waves in the waveguide of arbitrary cross section with anisotropic magnetoactive plate of finite thickness is considered. The wave equation for the potential of the transverse-magnetic (TM) field in the waveguide is received. The analytic method of solution of this equation is given. Fresnel formulas and power reflection and transmission coefficients for the plate are obtained.

articleTitle: Focusing properties of the elliptical type Fresnel lenses
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Geometrical configuration of elliptical type Fresnel lenses are considered. The problem of diffraction with use a method of the integral equations is numerically solved. In results of this decision, amplitude distributions of fields in focal area of lenses, their frequency properties are determined.

articleTitle: A different aproach to the singularity problem of boundary integral equations
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The numerical solution of boundary integral equations imply the integration of the kernel over the boundary which is singular in free space Greenpsilas function and its spatial derivatives when the point of interest coincides with the point of integration. In this paper we present a simple and efficient method for the singularity of the kernel. We introduce the weak form of Greenpsilas function by taking the spherical mean over the singular part of Greenpsilas function. Then we introduce its nonsingular gradient and gradient divergence operators. The convergences of the numerical solutions of integral equations are shown for simple objects.

articleTitle: Eigen waves of semi-opened waveguide structures
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The properties of the eigen waves of two waveguide structures are investigated in two cases: for semi-opened dielectric waveguide and for semi-opened elastic waveguide. It is proved that modes of semi-opened waveguides belonging to discrete and to continuous parts of spectrum form the orthogonal system.

articleTitle: Fractional boundary conditions in scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, we analyze some applications of the fractional boundary conditions (FBC) in the two-dimensional problems of wave reflection and diffraction. FBC are used to simulate reflection from dielectric slab where the fractional order depends on the layer parameters. The diffraction of an E-polarized electromagnetic field by a strip with FBC is studied. Numerical results are presented showing a comparison of the physical characteristics of the strip with FBC and impedance strip.

articleTitle: Radiation pattern calculation of flanged reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A technique for calculating radiation patterns of reflector antennas with curvilinear impedance peripheral flanges is presented. It is based on the uniform asymptotic theory with numerical diffraction coefficients and on the equivalent edge currents method. The use of numerical diffraction coefficients allows to account near-field terms in the incident field and nonuniform impedance distributions on the flange, provided that dimensions of the flange do not exceed several wavelengths.

articleTitle: Use of WEB-splines of arbitrary domain for waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: This paper illustrates the weighted extended b-splines as basis functions of finite element method of arbitrary domain for waveguides. This method does not need mesh generation for applications. The results are compared with the finite element method with triangulation method using Lagrange basis functions. This method can be used in more electromagnetic applications for future studies.

articleTitle: T-matrix method and singularities of analytical continuation of wave field
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The reason of limitations on scatterer geometry imposed by T-matrix method is ascertained. The condition of correctness of T-matrix method application is given. It is shown that at numerical solution of integral equations on the basis of null field condition, in particular at using T-matrix method it is necessary to take into account singularities of analytical continuation of wave field. Theoretical results are illustrated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Using method of integral equation on the base of cross region to solving three-dimentional difraction problems
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Using method of integral equations to solving three-dimensional diffraction problems are presented. The solution of three-dimensionally problem of radiation from longitudinal slot in wide wall of rectangular waveguide is considered.

articleTitle: Modeling of long-period fiber gratings with both refractive index and diameter modulation
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We present a mathematical model of long-period fiber gratings (LPFGs) which accounts for simultaneous perturbations of various parameters of the optical fiber: its refractive index and radius. We also present the results of the calculation of the cross-coupling between the fundamental mode of the fiber core and symmetric LP modes of the cladding as a function of the mode order, for the step-index optical fiber with harmonic modulation of the refractive index and radius both of the core and cladding.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic eigenwaves of planar layered metal-dielectric structure
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The dispersion equation for planar layered metal-dielectric structure are considered.

articleTitle: Regularization of complex beams
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The well known 2D complex-point-source beam presents undesired field characteristics. This paper proposes some combinations of simple complex beams which allow the construction of well behaved fields.

articleTitle: Mode basis method for open dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The paper considers generalization of Mode Basis Method on the case of open dielectric waveguides. Spectrum condensing was analyzed on the example of a rectangular waveguide with a dielectric layer when one of the walls is moved to infinity. At this the spectrum is partitioned into discrete (surface waves) and continuous (volume waves) parts. Some properties of this condensing were analyzed. Field expansion on such a nonuniform spectrum was illustrated numerically.

articleTitle: Boundary integral representation for time-harmonic Maxwell’s equations
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Method of weighted residual is used for developing of the boundary integral representation for Maxwell's equations. It is shown that the vectors of the electric and magnetic fields in an arbitrary point of domain can be expressed through its values on the boundary. The boundary integral equations of the second kind for the solving of the boundary-valued problems are received. It is marked that the given integral equation allows the effective numerical solving.

articleTitle: Through flattening-boundaries method to new square-gradient mechanism of surface scattering
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We develop the flattening-boundaries method to the problem of wave scattering in quasi-one-dimensional guiding systems with rough boundaries. This method allows one to reduce the problem to that describing the waveguide with flat boundaries and an effective scattering potential of a special structure. A detailed analysis of the potential reveals that apart from terms associated with well-known mechanisms of surface scattering, it contains important terms describing the square-gradient mechanism of scattering. These terms depend on the square of the derivative of the waveguide boundaries and in spite of their apparent smallness, they prevail in a physically important region of roughness parameters.

articleTitle: Excitation and observation of ball-lightning type spherical formations
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Experimental research results of discharge processes in liquids are presented. Excitation conditions of spherical plasma formation are met on the water-air boundary. Theoretical model of complex wave excited in layer media, is proposed to explain the plasmoid existence. It is shown that such structure can be formed by standing acoustic wave, which occurs during electrical discharge in water container.

articleTitle: Green function for the Maxwell system in chiral media using quaternionic analysis
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, the Green function for the Maxwell system in chiral media using quaternionic analysis is presented. Using the series expansion of the exponential function and the residue theory, fundamental solution of the operator M is obtained in explicit form.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of disprersive distortions of the wideband chirp signal during its propogation in the ionospheric radiochannel
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Theoretical description of the chirp ionosonde operation has been made. Ionosonde registers spectrum sequence of window received-signal sampling. Mathematical modeling of dispersive distortions of spectra registered has been carried out.

articleTitle: S-matrix of a two-port waveguide junction with triangular connecting cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: An H-plane triangle waveguide junction having arbitrarily triangular connecting cavity filled with dielectric is considered. In the cavity and waveguide arms, the field sought is expressed in the form of trigonometric series expansions which are constructed using the domain-product technique (DPT). The algorithm is applied to obtain a generalized scattering matrix of the unit.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of the material with negative refraction index
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The phenomenon of negative refraction is observed as multiple scattering of electromagnetic wave by the composite material with layers, which have different indices of refraction. It was shown that optical properties of such material strongly depend on the number of layers of such structure. The computer simulation has shown that the 35 layer propagation of the special periodically structures can give another direction of the propagation beam (oppositely Snell law).

articleTitle: Transmission line modelling method for planar boundaries containing positive and negative index media
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the planar boundaries containing positive and negative index media by using transmission line modeling method is presented. This method is based on the similarity between the basic equations for uniform plane waves propagating through the boundaries and waves traveling across the connections of transmission lines. At the end of the analysis, it is observed that the proposed method is easier, faster and more straightforward than the conventional method.

articleTitle: Dielectric function in semi-empirical tight-binding theory applied to crystalline diamond
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A semi-empirical tight-binding theory is employed to calculate the electronic band structure and the imaginary part of the dielectric function of crystalline diamond. Also, in order to validate the parameters used in this work, we have performed calculation by means of density functional theory with the local density approximation theory. We present the dependence of the dielectric function on the photon energy within two different approaches: interatomic and intra-atomic momentum matrix elements, which are applied and compared.

articleTitle: Conductivity of a Solid in a Strong Nonuniform State
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The necessity of a correction of the Chapman-Enskog method of construction of hydrodynamic equations in the case of kinetics of dilute electron gas in a solid has been shown. The strong spatially nonuniform states are investigated when collision integral of the considered kinetic equation must take into account an influence of nonhomogeneity of the system on collisions of particles. An usual expression for electric current in the system is corrected.

articleTitle: Intraocular pressure system inside vitreous humor
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Ocular pressure measurement is of great importance when we speak of glaucoma detection. When detected on time, blindness can be avoided on patients. The ocular pressure measurement is made by a MEMS device which is made basically of two parallel silicon plates with a diameter no longer than 800 microns, separated by a dielectric with estimated width of 5 microns. The pressure microsensor behaves in an adequate matter for our seaked goal, given that for small variations in pressure (Hg mm. units for human eye's case), there is also a change in the plate's deflection that can be measured.

articleTitle: Features of diurnal variability of aerosol optical depth over black sea
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Measurements of aerosol optical depth (AOD) are carried out within the framework of AERONET program. As of AOD conducted analysis of diurnal variability of transparency of atmosphere over Sevastopol with the aim to study characteristic of types of diurnal variability of aerosol optical depth for Black sea. For the determination of dominating type of the aerosol over Black sea was conducted comparative analysis of tinning data and results of similar studies at five specific land sites of AERONET, with regionally distributed aerosol types (urban, dust, dust and smoke, smoke, and background).

articleTitle: Trapped-mode resonances in optical planar metamaterials with metal elements
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Paper deals with analysis of the ldquotrapped moderdquo resonance properties in optical planar structures for metamaterials applications. The light diffraction solve algorithm for planar periodic metal-dielectric optical structures combines the mapped PSTD method with analytical transfer matrix method. The wavelength dependencies of reflection coefficients for periodic array with broken c-shaped and circle metal elements are presented.

articleTitle: Hohomogenization of periodic metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The methods of homogenization for periodic metamaterials or artificial media with periodic magnetodielectric, semiconductor, metallic, and cavity objects included in the background medium have been considered using the based on Greenpsilas functions integrodifferential equation methods.

articleTitle: Extraordinary optical transmission phenomena to the light of microwave field theory
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Unexpected enhanced transmission of electromagnetic waves through periodic arrays of electrically small holes or slits in opaque screens has been a hot topic of research during the last ten years. Most of work has been done in the frame of optics and condensed matter physics. At the present moment there is a well established theory explaining this phenomenon in terms of the so-called (spoof) surface plasmons. However, a simpler compatible point of view based on familiar concepts coming from classical microwave field and circuit theories is possible. This approach has the advantage of leading to simple reasonings able to predict the behavior of the perforated screens without resorting to tedious computation and/or complex theories. In this work we will show that the main physics of extraordinary transmission in 1D (arrays of slits and compound slits) and 2D (finite size holes arranged into square or rectangular lattices) systems is captured by simple equivalent circuit models. Moreover, the new approach allows us to state that extraordinary transmission is possible in systems without periodicity and in the absence of surface plasmons.

articleTitle: Interpolation algorithms of the non gaussian process at the output of the non linear non inertial converter
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: The sampling - reconstruction procedure (SRP) of a non Gaussian process at the output of the non linear non inertial converter driven by Gaussian process is considered. The type of the converter is exponential. The principal SRP characteristics (the reconstruction function and the error reconstruction function) are investigated for two different reconstruction algorithms. The first algorithm is based on the conditional mean rule. It provides the optimal the reconstruction function and the minimum of the error reconstruction function. The second algorithm is connected with the formulas for the Gaussian processes. This algorithm is no optimal. There is a comparison between both variants.

articleTitle: Guided modes and anomalous scatterign by a periodic lattice
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: We study a discrete prototype of anomalous electromagnetic scattering associated with the interaction of guided modes of a periodic scatterer and plane waves incident upon the scatterer.

articleTitle: Two ways for calculation of field evolution in dielectric waveguide: Via Brillouin- or eigen-waves
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Two complementary ways for calculation of an initial value problem in a dielectric waveguide is presented: Brillouin waves approach and eigenfrequency approach. The results show pure coincidence of two ways of calculation but the Brillouin approach is more intuitive and visual and makes less demands to computation resources.

articleTitle: Solution of the problem of electromagnetic pulses’ diffraction by variable separation method
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Variable separation method (VSM) allows to obtain an analytical solution for a very small number of boundary problems of wavespsila scattering by metallic and dielectric bodies, but it can be used to construct numerical solution for a wide enough range of boundary problems. In the present work the wave equation was solved in cylindrical and spherical coordinate systems. Obtained results have methodical novelty and can be used as an alternative to present methods of solving of non-stationary problems of diffraction on two-dimensional bodies.

articleTitle: Resonant scattering of electromagnetic waves by a PEC strip grating placed at the boundary of anisotropic dielectric
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Analytical regularization method is developed for the solution to boundary value problem of plane wave diffraction by PEC strip grating placed in the boundary of anisotropic dielectric. Extensive numerical investigation allowed obtaining profound insight of the complicated physical problem. Several promising for application effects have been found out and are to be discussed in presentation.

articleTitle: Use of quantum physics methods for study of propagation of electromagnetic waves in periodic media
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Notions and notations introduced in quantum physics can be of a big interest in electromagnetism to solve propagation and diffraction problems like propagation in periodic media.

articleTitle: Regularization of space-time integral equations for the problem of diffraction of electromagnetic pulses on slits
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: Space-time integral equations (IE) for the problem of diffraction of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) on slits in screens and on metallic stripes, located in bi-layer dielectrics, were obtained. IEs were solved by analytical transformation of logarithmic singularity of the kernel and application of collocation method. The singularity on the metallic edge was considered.

articleTitle: Pulse electromagnetic field scattering on a cone surfase with slots
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A model initial-boundary problem for a complex conical structure is considered. It is shown that the solution of this problem is equivalent to the solution of the algebraic equations system. The problem is solved by using rigorous methods. The longitudinal slots effects are studied.

articleTitle: Analytical regularization for diffraction problem: Open shell of revolution
publicationTitle: 2008 12th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory
abstract: A rigorous and numerically efficient approach for solving the scalar diffraction problem for open arbitrarily shaped shell of revolution is developed, when Dirichletpsilas boundary condition is imposed. The approach is based on the analytical regularization method. Seeking the solution by its integral representation, we determine the singular features of the kernel, and decompose it into the singular canonical part, and a regular remainder.
